uni-aero-core.title: Aerospace Engineering core
uni-aero-core.description: Core B.Tech aerospace engineering: aerodynamics, compressible flow, flight performance, propulsion and aircraft structures with solved numericals. Study companion; topics commonly taught in Indian B.Tech programmes.

lessons.title: Lab: Lift of a light aircraft in cruise

scenes.text: A trainee pilot at a flying club wants to know how much lift her trainer makes at 60 m/s.
The wing area is 16 m² and CL is 0.5 at sea level.

steps.title: Lift equation
steps.body: **L = ½ ρ V² S CL**. Dynamic pressure q = ½ρV². Sea-level ISA density is 1.225 kg/m³.

steps.title: Mistake
steps.body: Velocity is squared: doubling speed quadruples lift.

steps.title: Polar
steps.body: **CD = CD0 + CL²/(π e AR)**. The second term is induced drag.

courses.title: Flight mechanics: performance and manoeuvres
courses.summary: Rate of climb, Breguet range, turn performance and take-off distance.

lessons.title: Lab: Rate of climb from excess power

scenes.text: A pilot checks climb capability of a light aircraft before departing a high-altitude airfield.
The performance chart gives power available and power required.

steps.title: Excess power
steps.body: **RC = (Pa − Pr)/W** where Pa is power available, Pr power required and W weight.

steps.title: Altitude
steps.body: Power available falls with altitude for piston engines, so climb rate reduces.

scenes.text: A route planner needs the cruise range of a jet transport.

steps.title: Breguet (jet)
steps.body: **R = (V/c)(L/D) ln(W1/W2)** with c in 1/s (thrust-specific fuel consumption by weight).

steps.title: Lever
steps.body: Range grows with L/D and with fuel fraction.

scenes.text: A pilot rolls to 60° bank to turn onto final.

steps.title: Level turn
steps.body: **n = 1/cos φ** and **R = V²/(g√(n² − 1))**.

steps.title: Stall in turns
steps.body: Stall speed rises by √n in a turn.

scenes.text: A test cell measures an engine ingesting 50 kg/s at 200 m/s and exhausting at 600 m/s.
You verify the thrust.

steps.title: Thrust
steps.body: **T = ṁ(Ve − V0)** when exit pressure equals ambient and fuel mass is neglected.

steps.title: Mistake
steps.body: Include pressure thrust (pe − p0)Ae for rockets and choked nozzles.

steps.title: Worked example
steps.body: Ve/V0 = 3 gives ηp = 2/4 = 0.5.

steps.title: Insight
steps.body: Better efficiency comes from accelerating more air by less, which is why high-bypass fans dominate airliners.

steps.title: Ideal Brayton
steps.body: **η = 1 − 1/rp^((γ−1)/γ)**. Exponent is 0.2857 for air.

steps.title: Real engines
steps.body: Component losses and turbine inlet temperature limit actual efficiency.

courses.title: Aircraft structures: bending, buckling, load factors and pressurisation
courses.summary: Beam bending stress, Euler buckling, limit and ultimate loads and pressurised-fuselage stress.

scenes.text: A rectangular test spar 50 mm × 100 mm carries a bending moment of 2000 N·m.
You check the extreme-fibre stress.

steps.title: Flexure formula
steps.body: **σ = M y / I**, with I = b h³/12 for a rectangle.

steps.title: Mistake
steps.body: y is measured from the neutral axis (h/2 at the extreme fibre).

lessons.title: Lab: Euler buckling of a strut

scenes.text: A 1 m aluminium strut in a wing rib structure carries compression.
Will it buckle before it yields?

steps.title: Euler load
steps.body: **Pcr = π²EI/(KL)²**; K = 1 for pinned–pinned.

steps.title: Slenderness
steps.body: Valid only for long, slender members; short ones fail by yielding.

activity.prompt: E = 70 GPa, I = 4e-8 m⁴, L = 1 m, pinned ends. Critical load?

scenes.text: A designer follows the standard factor of safety of 1.5 on limit loads.
The limit manoeuvre factor is 3.8 g.

steps.title: Definitions
steps.body: Limit load is the maximum expected in service. **Ultimate = 1.5 × limit** for aircraft structures.

steps.title: Worked example
steps.body: n_limit = 3.8, n_ult = 5.7. With W = 10,000 N, ultimate load = 57,000 N.

steps.title: Rule
steps.body: Structure must carry limit loads without permanent deformation and ultimate loads without failure.

activity.prompt: Limit load factor 3.8, factor of safety 1.5. Ultimate load factor?

steps.body: Hoop stress **σh = p r / t**; longitudinal stress **σL = p r/(2t)**.

steps.title: Fatigue
